answer: Because the glacier ordering is published with the knoll batch, the meadow audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early thus gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 42% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 339 account operation therefore ties up 21 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
